lyrics:
[Intro: capoed acoustic guitar strum, same two high notes ringing]

[Verse 1: nasal drawl, guitar only]
Today was meant to be the day it turned around
By noon I'd lost the plot and half the town
I don't think there's anybody keeping score
But you're still standing in my door

[Verse 2: cello enters, lazy drum shuffle begins]
The word is out that I'm a fire going cold
I've heard it all before, it's getting old
I don't think anybody's told you yet
You're the only promise that I've kept

[Pre-Chorus: bass walks up, tambourine]
And all the maps I folded wrong
And all the songs I only half belong to
There's so much I keep meaning to say
But I trip on the words halfway

[Chorus: full band, piano doubles the tune]
So call it someday, call it soon
You're the window in a locked-up room
And after all the dark I put you through
You're my somedaylight

[Verse 3: full band, relaxed]
Tomorrow's got a way of running late
I've carried all this hope like extra weight
I don't think anybody stays the same
But you still answer to my name

[Pre-Chorus: bass walks up, tambourine]
And all the roads that bend away
And all the lights that lead us there are fading
There's so much I keep meaning to say
But I trip on the words halfway

[Chorus: full band, piano doubles the tune]
So call it someday, call it soon
You're the window in a locked-up room
And after all the dark I put you through
You're my somedaylight

[Instrumental: cello carries the melody, piano answers]

[Final Chorus: everyone, tambourine on every beat]
So call it someday, call it soon
You're the window in a locked-up room
And after all the dark I put you through
You're my somedaylight
I said you're my somedaylight

[Outro: band drops out, guitar and cello fade]
My somedaylight
Some day, light
Someday, right?
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 87 BPM, 4/4, F-sharp minor played with a capo so open strings ring. A loping, slightly behind-the-beat strum. Weary but hopeful.

VOICE: Nasal male tenor with a sneering drawl that stretches vowels at the end of lines. Single-tracked and dry in the verses, doubled in the chorus. Sung as if leaning on a wall.

INSTRUMENTS: Strummed acoustic guitar with a busy sixteenth-note right hand, the same two high notes ringing over every chord. A mournful cello line. Simple live drums with a lazy shuffle and lots of tambourine. Round electric bass that walks between sections. Upright piano doubling the chorus melody in octaves. Clean electric guitar adding the drone notes.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar alone, 4 bars. 0:11 Verse 1, voice and guitar. 0:33 Verse 2, cello and drums arrive together. 0:55 Pre-chorus. 1:17 Chorus 1, piano joins. 1:39 Verse 3. 2:01 Pre-chorus. 2:23 Chorus 2. 2:45 Instrumental, the cello sings the chorus tune. 3:07 Final chorus, with the last line repeated. 3:36 Outro, the band stops and guitar and cello fade out by 4:00.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-90s British rock: loud, dense and slightly overdriven on the mix bus, acoustic guitar pushed to the front, drums dry.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first chorus landing on the invented word, with the piano doubling it.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The narrator is no longer a young man waiting to be saved. He is older, has let people down, and is thanking the one who stayed. The three alternate hearings of the title are sung outright in the outro.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Shrugging defeat, gratitude admitted sideways, then said plainly.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

A man who keeps getting it wrong tells the one person still standing in his doorway what they are to him, using a word he had to invent.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: a partner who stayed; a child who makes a parent try again; sobriety; faith; or the home town you keep going back to. The invented word means whatever kept you going.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: an invented compound word as the title, vague time-words, a drawled second-person address, and four chords with ringing drone notes. Designed mishearing: 'somedaylight' splits into 'some daylight', 'Sunday light' and 'someday, right?', and all three work in the chorus.
